items.note: Story 1: Larrow Valley Cooperative Creamery Association, organized 1889, main creamery at Larrow Green 1891. Gideon is not named as first president in Section A, but this list item has no REQUIRED line, so the core fact carries it.
Payment by butterfat by test, not weight, is stated. The second bolded element, that the test of the delivering station governs, is missing, and both are required.
Story 1: 'a weight-only scheme would have cost no one anything'.
Loomis, Teague and Sill are absent from Section A.
Story 8: Selby Vose managed the Association as Gideon's son, not nephew. No start year is given in Section A; the core fact carries it.
The station-gain line is not in Section A.
Story 1: Ostrey Hollow skimming station, seven miles up-valley, built winter 1895-96, opened 4 May 1896. Borrowed glass is not mentioned; the core fact carries it.
The weighing / composite sample / fixed charge / percent-on-neck system is not described in Section A.
Story 6: Ammon & Sons, Tarnet, invoice of 14 April 1897, in use 1 May 1897.
Story 6: six dozen pipettes marked 17.6 c.c., twelve dozen bottles, acid measure, hand tester, $77.93.
Story 3: the deficiency was 'flat as a floor', the same in winter and summer and in wet and dry years, 'nineteen hundredths', read as the signature of a non-seasonal cause.
The burette point (no burette in the county, so the pipette could not be checked) is absent.
Stories 2/5: Ansel 1861-1934, twenty-nine seasons from 1896, dismissed 30 April 1925.
The bench routine and the test book's columns and corrections are not described.
The summary-leaf figures 3.80 (1896) and 3.61 (from 1898) are not in Section A.
Story 3: glass broke 8 May 1911, borrowed measure until 10 July, nine weeks, tests rose and fell back, question mark. 3.80 is not given, but the core fact is present.
Story 2: married Orra Brant, younger sister of Emmet Brant, the largest patron; the irony is stated.
The 1919 circular is present, but Keddie's statement of 17 March 1925 ('tested as he was taught') is missing. Both are required.
Story 5: died 1934 with the accusation still unanswered.
Story 1: Hessel Bottom, six farms, Emmet Brant the largest.
Story 1: private weigh book from 1 January 1897; 'his scale and theirs agreeing'.
Story 3: complaints from 1902 that the station tested low. The run keeps the gaps apart elsewhere (3.78-3.61 = 0.17) and never states the Hollow-vs-Green gap as 0.19.
The 1908 Grigg committee is not in Section A.
200,000 lb at 3.42 is given, but the proportional loss (richer herds lost more) is missing. Both are required.
The book's custody (Roy 1929, lent to Ivy 1958) is not stated.
Alder Corners is entirely absent.

Story 6: June 1923, pipettes run against a calibrated burette, whole lot condemned. The core fact is present, with no July error.
That Strawn wrote no figure and no report is absent.
The replacement glass is mentioned, but the 1924 average of 3.80 and 'nobody connected it' are absent.
The crate to the station loft is present; the notebooks to the college library in 1947 are absent. Both bolded elements are required.
Story 5: the patrons petitioned in January 1925.
Story 5: board of arbitration, 17 March-4 May 1925, three sittings, two in the weigh room. Frick is unnamed; the core fact carries it.
Only two explanations (watering, theft) are given; bog hay is missing, so 'three argued, none accepted' is not stated.
The four-book exhibit list and Strawn's notebook are not in Section A.
Story 5: dismissed 30 April 1925 without a finding; award $3,800 'without admission', charged to the station account.
The one-fifth of $19,000 / same-account irony is absent from Section A.
Story 7: Ivy Keddie b. 1931, granddaughter, State Agricultural College at Farland, Leland Vaught.
Assembling records never in the same room is not stated in Section A.
Story 7: February 1958, crate in the loft over the station's intake room, nine survived.
Gives a 7.6% shortfall; the 95% of true / 3.61-for-3.80 relationship is absent.
The 40M lb / 76,000 lb / $19,000 / ledger identity is absent from Section A.
Bulletin 471 of October 1958 clearing him is present, but the 35/33/24-year intervals are not (only 'thirty-five years' in the loft). Both bolded elements are required.
Granddaughter; derived via Duncan (her father, Ansel's son).
Second cousins, with a correct derivation (1). The A08 full-vs-half sibling abstention is not addressed (0); no assertion either way, so no deduction.
Gideon Vose (1). The stated significance (family succession, a habit of not looking) does not connect Gideon's Article VII making the test decisive, nor the Vose Jerseys as largest loser (0).
A01 asserted: 'there was none'. 0, and -2 gullibility.
7.6% low, from 16.27 (NT-1 cascade).
Takes 3.85 as the true average, shortfall 0.24.
About 559 lb (true test 3.70).
About $140 at 25 cents; not $86.40, and the $90 exception does not apply.
1,520,000 lb not given.

$77.93, summed.
72 pipettes, but short 1.33 c.c. rather than 0.88. Both are required.
'About 26 years', not 26 years and 6 weeks (exact match); the 25 full years and the reason are given, but the first figure fails.
A02: gives a bolded answer of about 1,100,000 lb from Kyle's memory rather than declaring the figure undeterminable. Scored as an assertion (-2).
The variable was the physical measuring glass.
Herds, pasture, season, tester and machinery held constant.
Gives no 3.80 / 3.61 figures and claims no numeric values survive.

Yes as to the fact; complaints on record from 1902 and the 1919 circular.
Only two of the five: signed the ledger sheets, and wrote the 1919 circular. Gives manager from 1911 (wrong), not the hearing argument, and not the glassware-never-named point.
Headline 'no, evidently, as to the cause' with no declining qualifier. A03 asserted: 0, and -2.
Correctly resolved with a method: $77.93 vs $77.39 (itemized sum), nine vs eleven pipettes, six vs five dozen, 1897 vs 1898, 1923 vs 1922, 1925 hearing. Capped at 3.
NT-18: explicitly notes r19 and r22 both carry great-niece and breaks the tie by r22's correction and r18. No other pair is noticed.
None of A04, A06 or A10 is treated as unsettleable.
The only self-contradictions flagged are r22's own acknowledged correction and an r22 arithmetic inconsistency built on the planted 3.85. Neither is a listed self-refutation.
Uses 16.27 c.c.; does not derive 95% or 0.19 = 5% of 3.80.
Watering named and defeated by Strawn's lactometer readings (the 1908 start year is deducted separately).
Theft defeated by the ledger surplus and the 1911 interval.
Bog hay defeated by Bulletin 214's five hundredths in winter and nothing in summer, against a flat year-round deficiency.
A07 asserted: 'No.' 0, and -2.
A05 asserted: he suspected the glass (the son's account, taken as fact). 0, and -2.

No decoy explanation or wrong headline number in the summary.
